source: Written 2026-10-22 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2026 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC26.ALR.GT.1: Pass B. Graphs are described in words by their vertices and edges, adjacency matrices by their rows, and tournaments by who beat whom (no pictures). Every claim about degrees, Euler routes, Hamiltonian routes, connected pieces and scores was re-derived by brute force in the generator. The small weighted-route question (nearest-neighbor circuit) states its rule in the stem, since the standard does not name weighted graphs. Two-step wins are defined in the stem wherever used.
notes.NC26.ALR.MDMF.2: 69 new questions. Systems are described in words (quota, weights of P1, P2, ...), coalitions as parenthesised lists. All keys, Banzhaf and Shapley-Shubik values, pivot and critical counts were computed by exhaustive enumeration in scripts/lib-b4-NC26.ALR.MDMF.2.mjs and asserted in build-b4-NC26.ALR.MDMF.2.mjs. Fairness of real systems is covered through weight-versus-power questions on described councils and boards (no named real systems or politics). No technology-based computation is tested; at most 5 players, with 24-order tables for 4 players.
notes.NC26.ALR.NQ.1: Pass B. Matrices are written in text by their rows (for example "rows [1, 2] and [3, 4]"), vectors as (3, -1). Matrix-valued answers are choice questions; numeric questions ask for one entry or a sum. Questions whose key is a square root of a perfect square have an empty compute (the checker has no square root). Every 2 by 2 inverse question either asks the student to apply the formula or supplies the inverse; no technology is needed. The inverse formula is not given except for the determinant ad - bc in some determinant questions.
notes.NC26.ALR.GT.2: Graphs are given as vertex and edge lists with weights (no pictures). Every key is recomputed by Kruskal, Prim, nearest-neighbor, cheapest-link, brute-force, greedy-coloring and critical-path routines in the build script, and weights are chosen so there are no ties. Critical path questions assume enough workers to run independent tasks at once, which each stem says. Only the TSP and coloring algorithms named in the standard are tested; no asymptotic or proof questions.
notes.NC26.ALR.L.1: Logic symbols are written in words (not p, p and q, p or q, if p then q, p if and only if q) as the brief requires, and gate inputs and outputs are 0 and 1. Every truth-table fact (counts of true rows, tautologies, contradictions, equivalences, circuit outputs) was verified by brute force in the generator script. 30 questions: 10 at each difficulty over truth values, negation and De Morgan, conditionals, converse/inverse/contrapositive, tautologies and contradictions, equivalence, validity of arguments and Boolean circuits.
notes.NC26.ALR.MDMF.1: All rankings are written as lists ("5 voters: A, B, C", first choice to last) and the rules are restated in the stem, so nothing needs a picture. Winners, counts and the three fairness examples (Condorcet, monotonicity of plurality with elimination, independence of irrelevant alternatives for the Borda count) are computed and checked by code in scripts/build-a4-NC26.ALR.MDMF.1.mjs. Arrow's theorem and defending a method are concept choice questions with one defensible option, since a proof of the theorem cannot be tested in text.
notes.NC26.ALR.MDMF.3: Every procedure is stated in the stem (sealed-bids settlement, the marker rule, what a chooser declares fair) so the key does not depend on one textbook's variant. Sealed-bid and marker keys are recomputed by routines in the build script. Everything is text only: the cake is described by values or by a one-dimensional cut. Playing out a whole method on a cake with continuous cuts for four or more players is not tested.
notes.NC26.ALR.MDMF.4: Populations are in thousands (or plain people counts), and every apportionment in the questions was computed with exact rational arithmetic in the generator (scripts/lib-a4-NC26.ALR.MDMF.4.mjs), including each tested modified divisor and the Huntington-Hill cutoffs, so there are no ties and no float rounding. 30 questions: 10 at each difficulty over the standard divisor and quota, Hamilton, Jefferson, Adams, Webster and Huntington-Hill, and fairness (quota rule, Alabama and population paradoxes, bias, average constituency). The Balinski-Young impossibility result and the new-states paradox are only touched in distractors and one solution.
notes.NC26.ALR.NQ.2: Matrices are written by their rows (no LaTeX matrix environments). Technology is not assumed: every inverse is a 2 by 2 done by hand, and Leslie/Markov questions use one or two steps or a steady state solved by a balance equation. Transition matrices use the row convention (row = current state), stated in the stem where it matters.
notes.NC26.ALR.NQ.3: Sets are written in plain-text braces such as {1, 2, 3} outside the maths, and set operations (union, intersection, complement) are written in words because set symbols are not allowed. 30 questions: 10 at each difficulty, covering sets and listing elements, subsets (including counting), union, intersection, complement, difference, counting elements of a union, two-set and three-set Venn problems, and De Morgan's law.
notes.NC26.ALR.NQ.4: Set equality is tested with sets written in plain braces and with set-builder conditions written in words or short inequalities; the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic is tested through factorization, factor counts and uniqueness. Arguments about primes, factors and parity are mostly choice questions about which argument or counterexample is valid, plus a few exact counting problems.

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has rows [2, 5] and [1, 3]. Matrix $B$ has rows [4, 1] and [0, 2]. What is the entry in row 1, column 2 of $A + B$?
questions.solution: To add matrices, add the entries in the same position. Row 1, column 2: $5 + 1 = 6$.

solve.work: A+B: row 1 col 2 = 5 + 1 = 6.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 2] and [3, 4], and let $B$ be the matrix with rows [5, 6] and [7, 8]. Which matrix is $A + B$?
questions.solution: Add the entries in matching positions: $1 + 5 = 6$, $2 + 6 = 8$, $3 + 7 = 10$, $4 + 8 = 12$. The matrix has rows [6, 8] and [10, 12].

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [9, 4] and [7, 6], and $B$ the matrix with rows [3, 1] and [2, 5]. What is the entry in row 2, column 1 of $A - B$?
questions.solution: Subtract the entries in the same position. Row 2, column 1: $7 - 2 = 5$.

solve.work: A-B row 2 col 1 = 7 - 2 = 5.

questions.stem: What is $3A$ when $A$ is the matrix with rows [1, -2] and [0, 4]?
questions.solution: Multiply every entry by 3: $3 \times 1 = 3$, $3 \times (-2) = -6$, $3 \times 0 = 0$, $3 \times 4 = 12$. The matrix has rows [3, -6] and [0, 12].

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: A matrix has 3 rows and 5 columns. How many entries does it have?
questions.solution: There are 5 entries in each of the 3 rows: $3 \times 5 = 15$.

solve.work: 3 rows x 5 columns = 15 entries.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: The size of a matrix is written rows by columns. Which pair of matrices can be added?
choices: a 2 by 3 matrix and a 3 by 2 matrix
a 2 by 3 matrix and a 2 by 2 matrix
a 2 by 3 matrix and a 2 by 3 matrix
a 3 by 2 matrix and a 3 by 3 matrix
questions.answer: a 2 by 3 matrix and a 2 by 3 matrix
questions.solution: Matrices can be added only when they have the same number of rows and the same number of columns. Only two 2 by 3 matrices match.

solve.answer: a 2 by 3 matrix and a 2 by 3 matrix
solve.work: Addition needs identical dimensions; only 2x3 and 2x3 match.

questions.stem: Let $u = (2, 3)$ and $v = (4, 1)$. What is the dot product $u \cdot v$?
questions.solution: Multiply matching components and add: $2 \times 4 + 3 \times 1 = 8 + 3 = 11$.

questions.stem: Let $u = (3, -1)$ and $v = (2, 5)$. Which vector is $u + v$?
questions.solution: Add matching components: $3 + 2 = 5$ and $-1 + 5 = 4$. So $u + v = (5, 4)$.

questions.stem: Which matrix is the 2 by 2 identity matrix?
questions.answer: rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]
questions.solution: The identity matrix has 1s on the main diagonal (top left to bottom right) and 0s everywhere else, so multiplying by it leaves a matrix unchanged. For 2 by 2 that is rows [1, 0] and [0, 1].

solve.answer: rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]
solve.work: The identity has 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere: rows [1,0],[0,1].

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: For a 2 by 2 matrix with rows [a, b] and [c, d], the determinant is $ad - bc$. What is the determinant of the matrix with rows [3, 2] and [1, 4]?
questions.solution: Here $a = 3$, $b = 2$, $c = 1$, $d = 4$. The determinant is $3 \times 4 - 2 \times 1 = 12 - 2 = 10$.

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has rows [1, 2, 3] and [4, 5, 6]. Matrix $B$ has rows [6, 5, 4] and [3, 2, 1]. Every entry of $A + B$ is the same number. What is it?
questions.solution: Add the entries in the same position. The first entries give $1 + 6 = 7$, and the other positions also give 7 ($2 + 5$, $3 + 4$, $4 + 3$, $5 + 2$, $6 + 1$).

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [2, -3] and [5, 0], and $B$ the matrix with rows [4, 1] and [-2, 3]. Which matrix is $A - B$?
questions.solution: Subtract the entries in matching positions: $2 - 4 = -2$, $-3 - 1 = -4$, $5 - (-2) = 7$, $0 - 3 = -3$. The matrix has rows [-2, -4] and [7, -3].

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has rows [4, -2] and [0, 6]. What is the sum of all four entries of $2A$?
questions.solution: Doubling every entry gives rows [8, -4] and [0, 12]. Their sum is $8 - 4 + 0 + 12 = 16$.

questions.stem: Adding the zero matrix to a 2 by 3 matrix leaves it unchanged. Which matrix is the 2 by 3 zero matrix?
questions.solution: The zero matrix has every entry 0, and it must be the same size as the matrix it is added to: 2 rows and 3 columns.

solve.work: 2 by 3 zero matrix: 2 rows of three 0s.

questions.stem: Every entry of the 2 by 2 matrix $A$ is 3. The matrix $I$ has rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]. What is the sum of all four entries of $A + I$?
questions.solution: $A + I$ has rows [4, 3] and [3, 4]. The entries add up to $4 + 3 + 3 + 4 = 14$.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: A matrix has 3 rows and 12 entries in all. How many columns does it have?
questions.solution: Each row has the same number of entries, so the number of columns is $12 \div 3 = 4$.

solve.work: 12 / 3 = 4 columns.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: What is the size, in rows by columns, of the matrix with rows [1, 2, 3, 4] and [5, 6, 7, 8]?
questions.answer: 2 by 4
questions.solution: The matrix has 2 rows, and each row has 4 entries, so it has 4 columns. The size is 2 by 4.

solve.answer: 2 by 4
solve.work: 2 rows, 4 columns: 2 by 4.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has 2 rows and 2 columns, and matrix $B$ has 2 rows and 3 columns. Which statement is true?
questions.answer: $AB$ is defined, but $BA$ is not
questions.solution: A product is defined when the columns of the first matrix equal the rows of the second. For $AB$: 2 columns and 2 rows, so it is defined. For $BA$: 3 columns and 2 rows, so it is not.

solve.answer: $AB$ is defined, but $BA$ is not
solve.work: A 2x2 times B 2x3: inner 2=2, defined. B 2x3 times A 2x2: inner 3 vs 2, not defined.

questions.stem: To find the entry in row 1, column 2 of a product $AB$, multiply row 1 of $A$ by column 2 of $B$: add the products of matching entries. Row 1 of $A$ is [3, 2], and column 2 of $B$ has entries 4 and 5. What is the entry?
Which statement tells how to find the entry in row 2, column 1 of the product $AB$?
choices: multiply row 1 of $A$ by column 2 of $B$
multiply row 2 of $A$ by column 1 of $B$
multiply row 2 of $B$ by column 1 of $A$
add row 2 of $A$ and column 1 of $B$
questions.answer: multiply row 2 of $A$ by column 1 of $B$
questions.solution: The entry in row $i$, column $j$ of $AB$ comes from row $i$ of the first matrix $A$ and column $j$ of the second matrix $B$: multiply matching entries and add. Here that is row 2 of $A$ and column 1 of $B$.

solve.answer: multiply row 2 of $A$ by column 1 of $B$
solve.work: Entry (2,1) of AB = row 2 of A times column 1 of B.

questions.stem: The matrix with rows [1, 2] and [3, 4] multiplies the column with entries 5 and 6. The result is a column with two entries. What is the second entry?
questions.solution: Use row 2, which is [3, 4]: $3 \times 5 + 4 \times 6 = 15 + 24 = 39$.

solve.work: Second entry = row 2 [3,4] dot (5,6) = 15 + 24 = 39.

questions.stem: Multiply matching components of $u = (1, 2, 3)$ and $v = (4, 5, 6)$, then add the three products. What is $u \cdot v$?
Let $u = (7, 0)$ and $v = (0, 9)$. What is $u \cdot v$?
What kind of object is the dot product of two vectors?
questions.answer: a single number
questions.solution: To find a dot product you multiply matching components and then add the products. The result is one number, not a vector or a matrix.

solve.answer: a single number
solve.work: The dot product is a scalar: a single number.

questions.stem: Let $u = (6, 2)$ and $v = (1, 5)$. Which vector is $u - v$?
questions.solution: Subtract matching components: $6 - 1 = 5$ and $2 - 5 = -3$. So $u - v = (5, -3)$.

questions.stem: The length of a vector $(a, b)$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. What is the length of the vector $(-7, 0)$?
questions.solution: $\sqrt{(-7)^2 + 0^2} = \sqrt{49} = 7$. A length is never negative.

questions.stem: Let $u = (4, -2, 6)$. Add the three components of the vector $\frac{1}{2}u$. What is the sum?
Let $I$ be the 2 by 2 identity matrix and $A$ any 2 by 2 matrix. Which statement is true?
questions.answer: $AI = A$
questions.solution: The identity matrix does for matrices what the number 1 does for numbers: multiplying by it leaves the matrix unchanged.

solve.answer: $AI = A$
solve.work: Identity: AI = A.

questions.stem: How many of the nine entries of the 3 by 3 identity matrix are equal to 0?
questions.solution: The identity matrix has 1s on the main diagonal, which is 3 entries, and 0s in the other $9 - 3 = 6$ places.

solve.work: 3x3 identity has 3 ones, 6 zeros.

questions.stem: Let $I$ be the 2 by 2 identity matrix. Which statement about $II$, the product of $I$ with itself, is true?
questions.answer: $II = I$
questions.solution: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged. Taking the matrix to be $I$ itself, $II = I$.

solve.answer: $II = I$
solve.work: II = I.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: The determinant of a 2 by 2 matrix with rows [a, b] and [c, d] is $ad - bc$. Find the determinant of the matrix whose rows are [5, 2] and [3, 1].
questions.solution: Here $a = 5$, $b = 2$, $c = 3$, $d = 1$. The determinant is $5 \times 1 - 2 \times 3 = 5 - 6 = -1$.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Multiplying the matrix with rows [2, 0] and [0, 5] by the matrix with rows [1/2, 0] and [0, 1/5] gives the identity matrix. What is the entry in row 2, column 2 of the inverse of the matrix with rows [2, 0] and [0, 5]?
questions.solution: Two matrices whose product is the identity are inverses of each other. So the inverse is the matrix with rows [1/2, 0] and [0, 1/5], and its row 2, column 2 entry is $\frac{1}{5}$.

solve.work: Inverse is [1/2, 0; 0, 1/5]; row 2 col 2 = 1/5.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: A 2 by 2 matrix has determinant 0. Which statement is true?
choices: Its inverse is the identity matrix
questions.answer: It has no inverse
questions.solution: A 2 by 2 matrix has an inverse exactly when its determinant is not 0, because the inverse formula divides by the determinant. Determinant 0 does not force every entry to be 0.

solve.answer: It has no inverse
solve.work: det 0 means not invertible.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [2, 1] and [3, 4], and $B$ the matrix with rows [1, 5] and [2, 0]. What is the entry in row 2, column 1 of the product $AB$?
questions.solution: Take row 2 of $A$, which is [3, 4], and column 1 of $B$, which is 1 and 2. Multiply matching entries and add: $3 \times 1 + 4 \times 2 = 3 + 8 = 11$.

solve.work: Row 2 of A is [3,4], column 1 of B is [1,2]: 3*1 + 4*2 = 11.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 2] and [0, 3], and $B$ the matrix with rows [2, 0] and [1, 1]. Which matrix is the product $AB$?
questions.answer: rows [4, 2] and [3, 3]
questions.solution: Row 1 of $A$ times the columns of $B$: $1 \times 2 + 2 \times 1 = 4$ and $1 \times 0 + 2 \times 1 = 2$. Row 2 of $A$: $0 \times 2 + 3 \times 1 = 3$ and $0 \times 0 + 3 \times 1 = 3$. So $AB$ has rows [4, 2] and [3, 3].

solve.answer: rows [4, 2] and [3, 3]

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 3 by 2 and matrix $B$ is 2 by 5 (rows by columns). Which statement about $AB$ is true?
questions.answer: $AB$ is defined and is 3 by 5
questions.solution: A product is defined when the number of columns of the first matrix equals the number of rows of the second. Here both are 2. The product has the first matrix's number of rows and the second matrix's number of columns: 3 by 5.

solve.answer: $AB$ is defined and is 3 by 5
solve.work: Inner dimensions 2 and 2 match, so AB is defined; size is 3 by 5.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrices $A$ and $B$ are both 2 by 3. Which statement is true?
choices: $AB$ is defined, but $A + B$ is not
$A + B$ is defined, but $AB$ is not
questions.answer: $A + B$ is defined, but $AB$ is not
questions.solution: The sum $A + B$ needs the same size, which they have. The product $AB$ needs the columns of $A$ (3) to equal the rows of $B$ (2), which they do not. So only $A + B$ is defined.

solve.answer: $A + B$ is defined, but $AB$ is not
solve.work: Same dimensions, so A+B is defined; AB needs columns of A (3) = rows of B (2), not equal, so AB undefined.

questions.stem: Let $u = (5, -2, 1)$ and $v = (-1, 4, 3)$. What is $u \cdot v$?
questions.solution: Multiply matching components and add: $5 \times (-1) + (-2) \times 4 + 1 \times 3 = -5 - 8 + 3 = -10$.

questions.stem: The length of a vector $(a, b)$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. What is the length of the vector $(6, 8)$?

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Which matrix is the inverse of the matrix with rows [2, 1] and [1, 1]?
questions.solution: The determinant is $2 \times 1 - 1 \times 1 = 1$. Swap the diagonal entries and change the signs of the other two: rows [1, -1] and [-1, 2], then divide by 1. Check: the product with the original is the identity.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Which matrix does not have an inverse?
questions.answer: rows [2, 4] and [1, 2]
questions.solution: A 2 by 2 matrix has an inverse only when its determinant $ad - bc$ is not 0. The determinants are 0 for the matrix with rows [2, 4] and [1, 2] ($4 - 4$), and 2, -3 and 9 for the others. So only the first has no inverse.

solve.answer: rows [2, 4] and [1, 2]
solve.work: Determinants: 2*2-4*1 = 0; 9; 1-4 = -3; 6-4 = 2. Only the first is singular.

questions.stem: Mia buys 4 of the first snack, 3 of the second and 2 of the third. They cost 25 cents, 50 cents and 125 cents each. With the vectors $q = (4, 3, 2)$ and $p = (25, 50, 125)$, the total cost in cents is $q \cdot p$. What is the total cost, in cents?
questions.solution: $q \cdot p = 4 \times 25 + 3 \times 50 + 2 \times 125 = 100 + 150 + 250 = 500$ cents.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 3] and [2, 0], and $B$ the matrix with rows [4, 1] and [5, 2]. What is the entry in row 1, column 2 of $2A - B$?
questions.solution: Row 1, column 2 of $2A$ is $2 \times 3 = 6$. Subtract the matching entry of $B$, which is 1: $6 - 1 = 5$.

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has rows [1, 2] and [0, 4]. Matrix $B$ is such that $A + B$ has rows [5, 3] and [2, 9]. Which matrix is $B$?
questions.answer: rows [4, 1] and [2, 5]
questions.solution: Subtract $A$ from the sum: $B = (A + B) - A$. The entries are $5 - 1 = 4$, $3 - 2 = 1$, $2 - 0 = 2$, $9 - 4 = 5$, so $B$ has rows [4, 1] and [2, 5].

solve.answer: rows [4, 1] and [2, 5]

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 0, -2] and [3, 4, 1], and $B$ the matrix with rows [2, 1, 1] and [0, -1, 3]. What is the entry in row 1, column 3 of $3A - 2B$?

The rows of a matrix are two stores and its columns are two items. In week 1 the sales matrix has rows [12, 8] and [5, 20]. In week 2 it has rows [9, 11] and [14, 6]. How many of item 2 did store 2 sell in the two weeks together?
questions.solution: Add the two matrices. Store 2 is row 2 and item 2 is column 2, so the entry is $20 + 6 = 26$.

solve.work: Store 2 item 2: 20 + 6 = 26.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrices $A$ and $B$ are both 4 by 3 (rows by columns). Which of these is NOT defined?
questions.answer: $AB$
questions.solution: Sums, differences and multiples are defined for matrices of the same size, which these are. A product $AB$ needs the columns of $A$ (3) to equal the rows of $B$ (4), which they do not.

solve.answer: $AB$
solve.work: 4x3 times 4x3: inner 3 vs 4, AB undefined; sums, differences and 2A are defined.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 3 by 4 and matrix $B$ is 4 by 2 (rows by columns). What is the size of $AB$?
questions.answer: 3 by 2
questions.solution: The 4 columns of $A$ match the 4 rows of $B$, so $AB$ is defined. It has the rows of $A$ and the columns of $B$: 3 by 2.

solve.answer: 3 by 2
solve.work: 3x4 times 4x2 = 3 by 2.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 2 by 3. For which size of matrix $B$ (rows by columns) are both $AB$ and $BA$ defined?
questions.answer: 3 by 2
questions.solution: For $AB$ the rows of $B$ must be 3, and for $BA$ the columns of $B$ must be 2. Only a 3 by 2 matrix does both.

solve.answer: 3 by 2
solve.work: AB needs B with 3 rows; BA needs B with 2 columns: B is 3 by 2.

questions.stem: Two matrices are $A$, with rows [2, -1] and [1, 3], and $B$, with rows [4, 1] and [2, 5]. Compute $AB$. What is the entry in its first row and second column?
questions.solution: Row 1 of $A$ is [2, -1] and column 2 of $B$ is 1 and 5. So $2 \times 1 + (-1) \times 5 = 2 - 5 = -3$.

solve.work: Row 1 of A [2,-1] dot column 2 of B (1,5) = 2 - 5 = -3.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [0, 1] and [1, 0], and $B$ the matrix with rows [3, 4] and [5, 6]. Which matrix is $AB$?
questions.answer: rows [5, 6] and [3, 4]
questions.solution: Row 1 of $A$ is [0, 1], so row 1 of $AB$ is $0 \times$ row 1 of $B$ plus $1 \times$ row 2 of $B$: [5, 6]. Row 2 of $A$ is [1, 0], so row 2 of $AB$ is row 1 of $B$: [3, 4]. Multiplying on the left by $A$ swaps the rows.

solve.answer: rows [5, 6] and [3, 4]
solve.work: A swaps the rows of B: AB = [5, 6; 3, 4].

questions.stem: The 2 by 3 matrix with rows [1, 2, 0] and [3, -1, 4] multiplies the column with entries 2, 1 and 5. The result is a column with two entries. What is the sum of those two entries?
questions.solution: First entry: $1 \times 2 + 2 \times 1 + 0 \times 5 = 4$. Second entry: $3 \times 2 + (-1) \times 1 + 4 \times 5 = 25$. The sum is $4 + 25 = 29$.

questions.stem: Which statement about multiplying two 2 by 2 matrices $A$ and $B$ is true?
choices: $AB$ is found by multiplying the entries in matching positions
$AB$ is found by adding the entries in matching positions
questions.answer: $AB$ and $BA$ can be different matrices
questions.solution: Matrix multiplication is not commutative. For example, with $A$ having rows [0, 1] and [1, 0] and $B$ having rows [1, 2] and [3, 4], $AB$ has rows [3, 4] and [1, 2], but $BA$ has rows [2, 1] and [4, 3]. And a product uses rows times columns, not matching positions.

solve.answer: $AB$ and $BA$ can be different matrices
solve.work: Matrix multiplication is not commutative: AB and BA can differ.

questions.stem: The vectors $u = (2, -3, 4, 1)$ and $v = (5, 2, -1, 6)$ each have four components. Find their dot product $u \cdot v$.

A student scores 80, 90 and 70 on three tests that count 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2 of the final grade. With $s = (80, 90, 70)$ and $w = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2)$, the final grade is $s \cdot w$. What is the final grade?
Two vectors are perpendicular when their dot product is 0. Which pair of vectors is perpendicular?
questions.solution: For $(2, 3)$ and $(3, -2)$: $2 \times 3 + 3 \times (-2) = 6 - 6 = 0$. The other pairs give 4, 13 and $-1$.

questions.stem: The length of a vector $(a, b)$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. What is the length of the vector $(20, 21)$?
Let $u = (1, -2, 3)$ and $v = (4, 0, -1)$. Which vector is $2u + v$?

A vector goes from the point $(2, 1)$ to the point $(11, 13)$. Its components are the changes in $x$ and in $y$. The length of a vector $(a, b)$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. What is the length of this vector?
questions.solution: The components are $11 - 2 = 9$ and $13 - 1 = 12$. The length is $\sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{81 + 144} = \sqrt{225} = 15$.

solve.work: Components (9, 12); length sqrt(81+144) = 15.

questions.stem: Let $I$ be the 2 by 2 identity matrix and $A$ any 2 by 2 matrix. Which expression is NOT always equal to $A$?
questions.answer: $A + I$
questions.solution: Multiplying by $I$ on either side leaves $A$ unchanged, so $AI$, $IA$ and $IAI$ all equal $A$. Adding $I$ changes the two diagonal entries, so $A + I$ is not $A$.

solve.answer: $A + I$
solve.work: IAI, AI, IA all equal A; A+I does not.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [2, 1] and [1, 1], which has an inverse. A matrix $X$ satisfies $AX = A$. Which matrix is $X$?
questions.answer: the 2 by 2 identity matrix
questions.solution: The identity matrix is the matrix that leaves $A$ unchanged when it multiplies it, so $AI = A$ and $X = I$. (Multiplying both sides by the inverse of $A$ gives the same result.)

solve.answer: the 2 by 2 identity matrix
solve.work: A invertible: multiply by A^-1, X = I.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: What is the determinant of the matrix with rows [6, -2] and [3, 5]? (For rows [a, b] and [c, d] it is $ad - bc$.)

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Which matrix is the inverse of the matrix with rows [1, 2] and [3, 7]?
questions.solution: The determinant is $1 \times 7 - 2 \times 3 = 1$. Swap the diagonal entries (1 and 7) and change the signs of the other two (2 and 3), then divide by 1: rows [7, -2] and [-3, 1].

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: For what value of $k$ does the matrix with rows [k, 6] and [2, 4] have no inverse?
questions.solution: A 2 by 2 matrix has no inverse when its determinant is 0. Here $4k - 12 = 0$, so $k = 3$.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Find the inverse of the matrix $A$ with rows [4, 3] and [2, 2]. What is the entry in the first row and second column of $A^{-1}$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $4 \times 2 - 3 \times 2 = 2$. The inverse is $\frac{1}{2}$ times the matrix with rows [2, -3] and [-2, 4], so its row 1, column 2 entry is $-\frac{3}{2}$.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: The system $2x + y = 7$ and $x + y = 4$ can be written $AX = B$. The inverse of $A$ has rows [1, -1] and [-1, 2], and $B$ is the column of 7 and 4. Multiplying $B$ on the left by the inverse of $A$ gives the column of $x$ and $y$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: The first entry of the result uses row 1 of the inverse: $1 \times 7 + (-1) \times 4 = 3$. So $x = 3$. (Then $y = -7 + 8 = 1$.)

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the 2 by 3 matrix with rows [1, 2, 3] and [4, 5, 6], and $B$ the 3 by 2 matrix with rows [1, 0], [0, 1] and [2, 3]. What is the entry in row 2, column 2 of $AB$?
questions.solution: Take row 2 of $A$, which is [4, 5, 6], and column 2 of $B$, which is 0, 1 and 3. Then $4 \times 0 + 5 \times 1 + 6 \times 3 = 0 + 5 + 18 = 23$.

solve.work: Row 2 of A [4,5,6] times column 2 of B [0,1,3] = 0 + 5 + 18 = 23.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 1] and [0, 1], and $B$ the matrix with rows [1, 0] and [1, 1]. Which matrix is $AB - BA$?
questions.solution: $AB$ has rows [2, 1] and [1, 1]. $BA$ has rows [1, 1] and [1, 2]. Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so they differ. Subtracting entry by entry, $AB - BA$ has rows [1, 0] and [0, -1].

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [3, 1] and [2, 4]. What is the entry in row 2, column 1 of $A^{-1}$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $3 \times 4 - 1 \times 2 = 10$. The inverse is $\frac{1}{10}$ times the matrix with rows [4, -1] and [-2, 3]. Row 2, column 1 is $\frac{-2}{10} = -\frac{1}{5}$.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: Which matrix is the inverse of the matrix with rows [3, 1] and [4, 2]?
questions.solution: The determinant is $3 \times 2 - 1 \times 4 = 2$. Swap the diagonal entries, change the signs of the other two, and divide every entry by 2: rows [2, -1] and [-4, 3] become rows [1, -1/2] and [-2, 3/2].

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: The system $3x + 2y = 12$ and $4x + 3y = 17$ can be written $AX = B$, where $A$ has rows [3, 2] and [4, 3], $X$ is the column of $x$ and $y$, and $B$ is the column of 12 and 17. Using $X = A^{-1}B$, what is $y$?
questions.solution: The determinant of $A$ is $3 \times 3 - 2 \times 4 = 1$, so $A^{-1}$ has rows [3, -2] and [-4, 3]. Then $y = -4 \times 12 + 3 \times 17 = -48 + 51 = 3$. (Also $x = 3 \times 12 - 2 \times 17 = 2$; check: $3 \times 2 + 2 \times 3 = 12$.)

questions.stem: Two vectors are perpendicular when their dot product is 0. For what value of $k$ is $u = (3, k)$ perpendicular to $v = (4, -6)$?
questions.solution: $u \cdot v = 3 \times 4 + k \times (-6) = 12 - 6k$. Setting this equal to 0 gives $6k = 12$, so $k = 2$.

questions.stem: Let $u = (2, -1)$ and $v = (0, 3)$. Which vector is $3u - 2v$?
questions.solution: $3u = (6, -3)$ and $2v = (0, 6)$. Subtract matching components: $6 - 0 = 6$ and $-3 - 6 = -9$. So $3u - 2v = (6, -9)$.

questions.stem: The vector $(a, 12)$, with $a > 0$, has length 13. Its length is $\sqrt{a^2 + 12^2}$. What is $a$?

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 2 by 3 and matrix $B$ is 3 by 2 (rows by columns). Which statement is true?
questions.answer: $AB$ is 2 by 2 and $BA$ is 3 by 3
questions.solution: $AB$ has the rows of $A$ and the columns of $B$: 2 by 2. $BA$ has the rows of $B$ and the columns of $A$: 3 by 3. Both are defined, because the inner sizes match in each case.

solve.answer: $AB$ is 2 by 2 and $BA$ is 3 by 3
solve.work: (2x3)(3x2) gives 2x2 for AB; (3x2)(2x3) gives 3x3 for BA. Both defined.

questions.stem: On Monday a bakery sells 10 rolls, 4 cakes and 6 pies. On Tuesday it sells 8 rolls, 5 cakes and 2 pies. A roll costs 2 dollars, a cake 5 dollars and a pie 3 dollars. Multiplying the matrix with rows [10, 4, 6] and [8, 5, 2] by the column of prices 2, 5 and 3 gives the money taken on each day. How many more dollars does the bakery take on Monday than on Tuesday?
questions.solution: Monday: $10 \times 2 + 4 \times 5 + 6 \times 3 = 58$ dollars. Tuesday: $8 \times 2 + 5 \times 5 + 2 \times 3 = 47$ dollars. The difference is $58 - 47 = 11$ dollars.

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has rows [1, 3] and [-2, 4], and matrix $B$ has rows [7, 5] and [0, 10]. The matrix $X$ satisfies $2X + A = B$. What is the sum of the four entries of $X$?
questions.solution: Solve for $X$: $2X = B - A$, which has rows [6, 2] and [2, 6], so $X$ has rows [3, 1] and [1, 3]. The entries add up to $3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8$.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [6, 3] and [0, 9], and $B$ the matrix with rows [0, -3] and [3, 3]. Which matrix $X$ satisfies $A - 3X = B$?
questions.solution: Rearrange: $3X = A - B$, which has rows [6, 6] and [-3, 6]. Divide every entry by 3: $X$ has rows [2, 2] and [-1, 2].

questions.stem: The rows of the matrix $P$ are two shops and its columns are two items. $P$ has rows [20, 35] and [15, 40]. A delivery matrix $D$ with rows [5, 0] and [10, 10] is added to the stock. Then 20% of everything is sold, so 80% (0.8 times each entry) remains. How many of item 1 remain in shop 2?
questions.solution: The new stock is $P + D$, with rows [25, 35] and [25, 50]. Shop 2 is row 2 and item 1 is column 1: 25 in stock. Then $0.8 \times 25 = 20$ remain.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 2 by 3, matrix $B$ is 3 by 4 and matrix $C$ is 4 by 2 (rows by columns). Which product is defined?
questions.answer: $ABC$
questions.solution: $AB$ is 2 by 4 (3 matches 3), and then $(AB)C$ is 2 by 2 (4 matches 4), so $ABC$ is defined. In $ACB$ the 3 columns of $A$ do not match the 4 rows of $C$. In $BAC$ the 4 columns of $B$ do not match the 2 rows of $A$. In $CBA$ the 2 columns of $C$ do not match the 3 rows of $B$.

solve.answer: $ABC$
solve.work: ABC: 2x3 . 3x4 . 4x2 defined. BAC: 3x4.2x3 no; CBA: 4x2.3x4 no; ACB: 2x3.4x2 no.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 3 by $n$ and matrix $B$ is 5 by 2. The product $AB$ is defined. How many entries does $AB$ have?
questions.solution: The product is defined only when the columns of $A$ equal the rows of $B$, so $n = 5$. Then $AB$ is 3 by 2, which has $3 \times 2 = 6$ entries.

solve.work: Defined needs n = 5; AB is 3 by 2: 6 entries.

questions.skill: Matrix size and when operations are defined
questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is 3 by 3 and matrix $B$ is a column with 3 entries (3 by 1). Which statement is true?
choices: $AB$ is defined and is 3 by 1, but $BA$ is not defined
$BA$ is defined and is 3 by 3, but $AB$ is not defined
$AB$ and $BA$ are both defined and both are 3 by 3
$AB$ and $BA$ are both defined and both are 3 by 1
questions.answer: $AB$ is defined and is 3 by 1, but $BA$ is not defined
questions.solution: $AB$: the 3 columns of $A$ match the 3 rows of $B$, and the result is 3 by 1. $BA$: the 1 column of $B$ does not match the 3 rows of $A$, so it is not defined.

solve.answer: $AB$ is defined and is 3 by 1, but $BA$ is not defined
solve.work: 3x3 times 3x1 = 3x1; 3x1 times 3x3: inner 1 vs 3, undefined.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 0, 2], [0, 3, 1] and [2, 1, 0], and $B$ the matrix with rows [1, 1, 0], [2, 0, 1] and [0, 3, 1]. The main diagonal of $AB$ is its entries in row 1 column 1, row 2 column 2 and row 3 column 3. What is the sum of those three entries?
questions.solution: Row 1 of $A$ times column 1 of $B$: $1 + 0 + 0 = 1$. Row 2 times column 2: $0 + 0 + 3 = 3$. Row 3 times column 3: $0 + 1 + 0 = 1$. The sum is $1 + 3 + 1 = 5$.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [0, 1] and [-1, 0]. Which matrix is $A^2 = AA$?
questions.solution: Row 1 of $A$ is [0, 1]: times column 1 (0 and -1) gives $-1$, times column 2 (1 and 0) gives 0. Row 2 is [-1, 0]: times column 1 gives 0, times column 2 gives $-1$. So $A^2$ has rows [-1, 0] and [0, -1]. Squaring the entries one by one would be a mistake.

questions.stem: Let $A$ be the matrix with rows [1, 2] and [0, 1]. What is the entry in row 1, column 2 of $A^4 = AAAA$?
questions.solution: $A^2 = AA$ has rows [1, 4] and [0, 1]. Then $A^4 = A^2 A^2$: row 1, column 2 is $1 \times 4 + 4 \times 1 = 8$. (Its rows are [1, 8] and [0, 1].)

questions.stem: Ana makes 3 tables and 2 chairs a day. Ben makes 1 table and 4 chairs a day. A table earns 40 dollars and a chair earns 15 dollars. Multiplying the matrix with rows [3, 2] and [1, 4] by the column of earnings 40 and 15 gives what each person earns in a day. How many more dollars does Ana earn in a day than Ben?
questions.solution: Ana: $3 \times 40 + 2 \times 15 = 150$ dollars. Ben: $1 \times 40 + 4 \times 15 = 100$ dollars. The difference is $150 - 100 = 50$ dollars.

questions.stem: Let $u = (k, 2, 3)$ and $v = (4, -1, 2)$. The dot product $u \cdot v$ is 14. What is $k$?
questions.solution: $u \cdot v = 4k + 2 \times (-1) + 3 \times 2 = 4k + 4$. Setting $4k + 4 = 14$ gives $4k = 10$, so $k = 2.5$.

questions.stem: Two vectors are perpendicular when their dot product is 0. Which vector is perpendicular to $(4, -3)$?
The vector $(a, 2a)$, with $a > 0$, has dot product 45 with itself. What is $a$?
questions.solution: $(a, 2a) \cdot (a, 2a) = a^2 + 4a^2 = 5a^2$. Setting $5a^2 = 45$ gives $a^2 = 9$, and since $a > 0$, $a = 3$.

questions.stem: A vector goes from the point $(-3, 5)$ to the point $(5, -10)$. Its components are the changes in $x$ and in $y$, and the length of a vector $(a, b)$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. What is its length?
questions.solution: The components are $5 - (-3) = 8$ and $-10 - 5 = -15$. The length is $\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{64 + 225} = \sqrt{289} = 17$.

solve.work: Components (8, -15); length sqrt(64+225) = 17.

questions.stem: Let $u = (3, 1)$ and $v = (4, -2)$. Which vector $w$ satisfies $u + w = 2v$?
Dividing the vector $(9, 12)$ by its length gives a vector of length 1. The length of $(a, b)$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$. What is the first component of that vector?
questions.solution: The length is $\sqrt{81 + 144} = 15$. Dividing each component by 15 gives $(\frac{9}{15}, \frac{12}{15}) = (\frac{3}{5}, \frac{4}{5})$. The first component is $\frac{3}{5}$.

solve.work: Length 15; first component 9/15 = 3/5.

questions.stem: Let $I$ be the 2 by 2 identity matrix. Which matrix $X$ satisfies $X + I = $ the matrix with rows [3, 1] and [0, 4]?
questions.answer: rows [2, 1] and [0, 3]
questions.solution: Subtract $I$, which has rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]: $X = $ rows [3 - 1, 1 - 0] and [0 - 0, 4 - 1] = rows [2, 1] and [0, 3]. Only the diagonal entries change.

solve.answer: rows [2, 1] and [0, 3]

questions.stem: Let $I$ be the 3 by 3 identity matrix and $B = 3I$. What is the sum of all nine entries of $B^2 = BB$?
questions.solution: $B^2 = (3I)(3I) = 9II = 9I$. The matrix $9I$ has 9 on its three diagonal places and 0 elsewhere, so the sum is $3 \times 9 = 27$.

solve.work: B^2 = 9I; sum of entries 27.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: For $x > 0$, the matrix with rows [x + 1, 6] and [2, x] has no inverse. What is $x$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $(x + 1)x - 6 \times 2 = x^2 + x - 12$, which is $(x + 4)(x - 3)$. It is 0 for $x = 3$ or $x = -4$. Since $x > 0$, $x = 3$.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: The matrix $M$ has rows [2, -1] and [4, 3]. Which matrix is $M^{-1}$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $2 \times 3 - (-1) \times 4 = 6 + 4 = 10$. Swap the diagonal entries and change the signs of the other two: rows [3, 1] and [-4, 2]. Then divide every entry by 10: rows [3/10, 1/10] and [-2/5, 1/5].

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: The system $5x + 2y = 19$ and $2x + y = 8$ can be written $AX = B$ with $A$ having rows [5, 2] and [2, 1]. Solve it by using the inverse of $A$. What is $y$?
questions.solution: The determinant of $A$ is $5 \times 1 - 2 \times 2 = 1$, so $A^{-1}$ has rows [1, -2] and [-2, 5]. Then $y = (-2) \times 19 + 5 \times 8 = -38 + 40 = 2$. (Check: $x = 19 - 16 = 3$, and $5 \times 3 + 2 \times 2 = 19$.)

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: The inverse of the matrix $A$ is the matrix with rows [3, 2] and [4, 3]. What is the entry in row 2, column 1 of $A$?
questions.solution: The inverse of the inverse is the original matrix. The matrix with rows [3, 2] and [4, 3] has determinant $9 - 8 = 1$, so its inverse has rows [3, -2] and [-4, 3]. Row 2, column 1 is $-4$.

questions.skill: Determinants and inverses of 2 by 2 matrices
questions.stem: A message column $X$ is coded by multiplying by $M$, the matrix with rows [3, 2] and [1, 1]. The coded column is 14 and 6. The inverse of $M$ has rows [1, -2] and [-1, 3]. What is the second entry of the original column $X$?
questions.solution: Decode with the inverse: $X = M^{-1}$ times the coded column. The second entry uses row 2 of the inverse: $(-1) \times 14 + 3 \times 6 = -14 + 18 = 4$. (The first entry is $14 - 12 = 2$.)

questions.stem: A bakery's price matrix is the row matrix $[3, 2]$: a muffin costs 3 dollars and a cookie costs 2 dollars. Maria's order is the column matrix with entries $4$ (muffins) and $5$ (cookies). The product of the row matrix and the column matrix is a $1\times1$ matrix. What is its single entry, in dollars?
questions.solution: Multiply the matching entries and add: $3\times4+2\times5=12+10=22$.

questions.stem: A matrix records how many of each of 2 products were sold by each of 3 stores. It has one row for each store and one column for each product. What is its size (rows by columns)?
questions.answer: $3\times2$
questions.solution: There are 3 stores, so 3 rows, and 2 products, so 2 columns. The size is $3\times2$.

solve.answer: $3\times2$
solve.work: 3 stores = 3 rows, 2 products = 2 columns: 3x2.

questions.stem: For a $2\times2$ matrix with rows $[a, b]$ and $[c, d]$, the determinant is $ad-bc$. What is the determinant of the matrix with rows $[5, 2]$ and $[3, 4]$?
questions.solution: $ad-bc=5\times4-2\times3=20-6=14$.

questions.stem: Which of these $2\times2$ matrices has no inverse?
questions.solution: A matrix has no inverse when its determinant is 0. For rows $[2, 4]$ and $[1, 2]$: $2\times2-4\times1=0$. The others have determinants $1$, $-1$ and $5$.

solve.work: Determinants: 8-3=5; 4-4=0; 5-6=-1; 3-2=1. Only [2,4],[1,2] has determinant 0.

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: The system $2x+y=5$ and $x+y=3$ is written as $AX=B$, where $X$ is the column with entries $x$ and $y$. What is the coefficient matrix $A$?
questions.solution: The coefficients of $x$ and $y$ in each equation form a row: $[2, 1]$ from the first equation and $[1, 1]$ from the second. The constants 5 and 3 go in $B$.

solve.work: Coefficients of x and y: row 1 [2,1], row 2 [1,1].

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: The system $x+y=7$ and $x+2y=10$ is written as $AX=B$, where $A$ has rows $[1, 1]$ and $[1, 2]$ and $B$ is the column with entries $7$ and $10$. The inverse of $A$ has rows $[2, -1]$ and $[-1, 1]$. Find $x$, the first entry of $X=A^{-1}B$.
questions.solution: The first entry of $A^{-1}B$ is $2\times7+(-1)\times10=14-10=4$. (Check: $x=4$, $y=3$ gives $x+y=7$ and $x+2y=10$.)

questions.stem: In a Leslie matrix for a population with several age classes, what do the entries of the top row represent?
choices: The fraction of each age class that survives to the next age class
The number of individuals in each age class at the start
The average number of offspring per individual in each age class
The fraction of each age class that dies during the year
questions.answer: The average number of offspring per individual in each age class
questions.solution: The top row gives the fertility of each age class: how many offspring, on average, each individual of that age produces. The survival fractions are on the diagonal just below the main diagonal.

solve.answer: The average number of offspring per individual in each age class
solve.work: Top row of a Leslie matrix holds fecundities: average offspring per individual of each age class.

questions.stem: A population has two age classes, young and adult. Its Leslie matrix has rows $[0, 3]$ and $[0.5, 0]$: each adult produces 3 young per year, and half of the young survive to become adults. This year there are 40 young and 20 adults. How many young will there be next year?
questions.solution: Next year's young come only from this year's adults: $0\times40+3\times20=60$.

solve.work: Young next year = 0*40 + 3*20 = 60.

questions.stem: In a Markov chain, the transition matrix has one row for each current state, and the entries of a row give the probabilities of moving to each state next. Which statement is true of every row?
choices: The entries are between 0 and 1 and add up to the number of states
The entries are between 0 and 1 and the largest entry is always 1
The entries are between 0 and 1 and are all equal to each other
The entries are between 0 and 1 and add up to 1
questions.answer: The entries are between 0 and 1 and add up to 1
questions.solution: From any state the chain must go somewhere, so the probabilities in a row cover every possibility and add up to 1.

solve.answer: The entries are between 0 and 1 and add up to 1
solve.work: Each row is a probability distribution over next states, so entries in [0,1] summing to 1.

questions.stem: A day is either sunny or rainy. The transition matrix has rows $[0.9, 0.1]$ (from a sunny day) and $[0.4, 0.6]$ (from a rainy day), with the columns in the order sunny, rainy. If today is rainy, what is the probability that tomorrow is sunny?
questions.solution: Use the row for a rainy day, $[0.4, 0.6]$. The first column is sunny, so the probability is $0.4$.

solve.work: Row 'from rainy' = [0.4, 0.6]; sunny column = 0.4.

questions.stem: In a school store, the row matrix $[6, 4]$ shows how many pencils and erasers one student buys. The column matrix with entries $50$ and $25$ shows the price of one pencil and of one eraser, in cents. Multiplying the row matrix by the column matrix gives a $1\times1$ matrix, the total cost. What is its entry, in cents?
questions.solution: Multiply matching entries and add: $6\times50+4\times25=300+100=400$ cents.

questions.stem: A matrix records the points that 4 players scored in each of 3 rounds, with one row for each player and one column for each round. Which description of the matrix is correct?
questions.answer: 4 by 3, with 12 entries
questions.solution: One row per player gives 4 rows, and one column per round gives 3 columns. A 4 by 3 matrix has $4\times3=12$ entries.

solve.answer: 4 by 3, with 12 entries
solve.work: 4 rows (players) by 3 columns (rounds) = 4 by 3, 12 entries.

questions.stem: The matrix $T$ has rows [12, 8, 5], [9, 11, 7] and [4, 6, 10]. It shows the stock of 3 products in 3 stores, with one row for each store and one column for each product. What does the entry $7$, in row 2 and column 3, tell us?
questions.answer: Store 2 has 7 of product 3
questions.solution: Row 2 is store 2 and column 3 is product 3, so the entry 7 is the stock of product 3 in store 2.

solve.answer: Store 2 has 7 of product 3
solve.work: Row 2 = store 2, column 3 = product 3.

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ has 3 rows and 4 columns, and matrix $B$ has 4 rows and 2 columns. How many entries does the product $AB$ have?
questions.solution: The product is defined because $A$ has 4 columns and $B$ has 4 rows. $AB$ has the rows of $A$ and the columns of $B$: 3 rows and 2 columns, so $3\times2=6$ entries.

solve.work: (3x4)(4x2) = 3x2, 6 entries.

questions.stem: The determinant of a 2 by 2 matrix with rows [a, b] and [c, d] is $ad - bc$. What is the determinant of the matrix with rows [6, -2] and [3, 4]?
A 2 by 2 matrix has an inverse exactly when its determinant is
choices: greater than 0, so it must be positive
equal to 1, like the identity matrix
different from 0, whether it is positive or negative
equal to 0, so that it cancels out
questions.answer: different from 0, whether it is positive or negative
questions.solution: The inverse formula divides by the determinant, so the determinant cannot be 0. Any other value, positive or negative, works.

solve.answer: different from 0, whether it is positive or negative
solve.work: Invertible iff det is nonzero.

questions.stem: When a matrix is multiplied by its inverse, the result is
choices: the zero matrix, with rows [0, 0] and [0, 0]
the matrix of all ones, with rows [1, 1] and [1, 1]
the identity matrix, with rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]
questions.answer: the identity matrix, with rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]
questions.solution: An inverse undoes the matrix, like dividing by a number. Matrix times inverse is the identity matrix, which has 1 on the diagonal and 0 elsewhere.

solve.answer: the identity matrix, with rows [1, 0] and [0, 1]

questions.stem: For a 2 by 2 matrix with rows [a, b] and [c, d] whose determinant is 1, the inverse has rows [d, -b] and [-c, a]. The matrix $A$ has rows [3, 1] and [5, 2]. What is the entry in row 1, column 2 of $A^{-1}$?
questions.solution: Here $a=3$, $b=1$, $c=5$, $d=2$ and the determinant is $3\times2-1\times5=1$. Row 1, column 2 of the inverse is $-b=-1$.

solve.work: det = 3x2 - 1x5 = 1; inverse rows [2,-1],[-5,3]; row 1 col 2 = -1.

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: The system $3x + 2y = 12$ and $x + y = 5$ is written $AX = B$, where $A$ has rows [3, 2] and [1, 1], $X$ has entries $x$ and $y$, and $B$ has entries 12 and 5. The inverse of $A$ has rows [1, -2] and [-1, 3]. Find $y$.
questions.solution: $X=A^{-1}B$. The second entry uses row 2 of the inverse: $y=(-1)\times12+3\times5=3$. (Then $x=12-10=2$, and $3\times2+2\times3=12$.)

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: The system $4x - y = 7$ and $2x + 3y = 1$ is written as $AX = B$, where $X$ has entries $x$ and $y$. Which matrix is the coefficient matrix $A$?
questions.solution: Each row of $A$ holds the coefficients of $x$ and $y$ from one equation: [4, -1] from the first and [2, 3] from the second. The right-hand sides 7 and 1 go in $B$.

solve.work: Coefficients: [4,-1],[2,3].

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: A matrix equation $AX = B$ has an invertible matrix $A$. Which step solves it for $X$?
choices: multiply both sides on the right by $A^{-1}$, giving $X = BA^{-1}$
multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$, giving $X = A^{-1}B$
divide each entry of $B$ by the matching entry of $A$
subtract $A$ from both sides, giving $X = B - A$
questions.answer: multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$, giving $X = A^{-1}B$
questions.solution: $A^{-1}(AX)=(A^{-1}A)X=X$, so multiply both sides by the inverse on the left. The order matters because matrix multiplication is not commutative.

solve.answer: multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$, giving $X = A^{-1}B$
solve.work: Left-multiply by A^-1: X = A^-1 B.

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: The matrix equation $AX = B$ has $B$ with entries 8 and 5. The inverse of $A$ has rows [1, -1] and [-2, 3]. What is the second entry of $X = A^{-1}B$?
questions.solution: Use row 2 of the inverse: $(-2)\times8+3\times5=-16+15=-1$.

solve.work: Second entry = -2 x 8 + 3 x 5 = -16 + 15 = -1.

questions.stem: In a Leslie matrix, the entry in row 3, column 2 is not in the top row. What does it represent?
choices: the number of offspring produced by each member of age class 3
the fraction of age class 3 that dies during the year
the fraction of age class 2 that survives to become age class 3
the number of offspring produced by each member of age class 2
questions.answer: the fraction of age class 2 that survives to become age class 3
questions.solution: Only the top row holds birth rates. An entry just below the diagonal in row $k+1$, column $k$ is the survival fraction from age class $k$ to age class $k+1$. Here $k=2$.

solve.answer: the fraction of age class 2 that survives to become age class 3
solve.work: Subdiagonal entry (3,2) = survival fraction from class 2 to class 3.

questions.stem: A beetle population has larvae and adults. Each year every adult produces 5 larvae and then dies, and 20 percent of the larvae become adults. Now there are 100 larvae and 30 adults. How many larvae will there be next year?
questions.solution: Only adults produce larvae: $5\times30=150$ larvae. (There will be $0.2\times100=20$ adults.)

solve.work: Larvae next year come only from adults: 5 x 30 = 150.

questions.stem: A population has two age classes, young and adult, listed in that order. Each year every adult has 3 young, and 40 percent of the young become adults. Adults die at the end of the year. Which is the Leslie matrix?
questions.solution: The top row holds births: the young come from the adults, so the entry in column 2 is 3 and the entry in column 1 is 0. The second row holds survival: 0.4 of the young become adults, so the entry in column 1 is 0.4, and adults do not survive, so the entry in column 2 is 0.

solve.work: Top row fecundities [0,3]; survival young->adult 0.4 in row 2 col 1: [0.4,0].

questions.stem: A population has three age classes. Each year, 0.5 of class 1 survive to class 2, and 0.2 of class 2 survive to class 3. Class 3 animals do not survive the year. Now the classes hold 200, 80 and 40 animals. How many animals will be in class 3 next year?
questions.solution: Only class 2 animals can become class 3: $0.2\times80=16$.

solve.work: Class 3 next = 0.2 x 80 = 16.

questions.stem: One row of a transition matrix for a Markov chain with three states is [0.25, ?, 0.35]. What number is the ?
questions.solution: The probabilities in a row add to 1, so $?=1-0.25-0.35=0.4$.

solve.work: Row of a (row-stochastic) transition matrix sums to 1: 1 - 0.25 - 0.35 = 0.4.

questions.stem: Each month, one fifth of the riders on bus route P switch to route Q, and nobody switches from Q to P. This month 300 riders use route P and 100 use route Q. How many riders will use route Q next month?
questions.solution: One fifth of 300 is 60 riders who switch, so route Q has $100+60=160$ riders.

questions.stem: A Markov chain has states A, B and C, in that order. The entry in row $i$, column $j$ of its transition matrix is the probability of moving from state $i$ to state $j$. Which entry is the probability of moving from C to A?
questions.answer: row 3, column 1
questions.solution: The row names the state you start in (C is the third state) and the column names the state you move to (A is the first state), so row 3, column 1.

solve.answer: row 3, column 1
solve.work: From C (row 3) to A (column 1).

questions.stem: A Markov chain with two states has transition matrix with rows [0.6, 0.4] and [0.3, 0.7]. The probability vector $(p, q)$ gives the chances of being in state 1 and state 2, and one step later it is $(p, q)$ times the matrix. At first the chances are $(0.5, 0.5)$. What is the probability of being in state 1 after one step?
questions.solution: Reach state 1 from state 1 (probability $0.5\times0.6$) or from state 2 (probability $0.5\times0.3$): $0.30+0.15=0.45$.

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: A matrix model of a rectangular garden gives $X = A^{-1}B$ as the column with entries 6 and 9, the width and the length in meters. How many meters of fence go all the way around the garden?
questions.solution: The width is 6 and the length is 9, so the distance around is $2\times(6+9)=30$ meters.

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: Ana solves a matrix model for the width and the length of a garden and gets a width of 6 meters and a length of $-2$ meters. What does the $-2$ tell her?
choices: The garden is 2 meters long but faces the opposite direction
The garden is 2 meters shorter than it is wide
The answer is impossible, so she should recheck the model, since a length cannot be negative
The garden has no area, since one entry is negative
questions.answer: The answer is impossible, so she should recheck the model, since a length cannot be negative
questions.solution: A length is a distance, so it cannot be negative. A negative entry shows that the setup or the arithmetic has an error, or that no such garden exists.

solve.answer: The answer is impossible, so she should recheck the model, since a length cannot be negative
solve.work: A negative length is impossible in context; recheck the model.

questions.stem: A Markov chain models the weather. State 1 is sunny and state 2 is rainy. Its transition matrix has rows [0.8, 0.2] and [0.4, 0.6], and each row gives the probabilities for tomorrow's weather given today's. If today is rainy, what is the probability that tomorrow is sunny?
questions.solution: Today is rainy, which is state 2, so use row 2: [0.4, 0.6]. The first entry is the probability of moving to state 1, sunny. So the probability is 0.4. (0.6 is the chance that it stays rainy.)

solve.work: Row 2 (rainy today) is [0.4, 0.6]; the entry for sunny tomorrow is 0.4.

questions.stem: The matrix $S$ shows how many of each of 3 items were sold by each of 2 stores, with one row for each store and one column for each item. A matrix $P$ lists the price of each item so that the product $SP$ gives the revenue of each store. What size must $P$ be?
questions.answer: $3\times1$
questions.solution: $S$ is $2\times3$, so $P$ needs 3 rows to match. One column of prices gives one revenue per store: $SP$ is $2\times1$. So $P$ is $3\times1$.

solve.answer: $3\times1$
solve.work: S is 2x3; SP must be defined and give one revenue per store, so P is 3x1 (SP is 2x1).

questions.stem: A kitchen has two recipes. The matrix $R$ has rows $[3, 1]$ (cake) and $[2, 2]$ (pie); the columns are cups of flour and cups of sugar used per item. The row matrix $[4, 5]$ gives the number of cakes and pies baked. The product $[4, 5]R$ gives the total cups of flour and sugar used. How many cups of sugar are used?
questions.solution: The sugar total is the second entry of the product: $4\times1+5\times2=4+10=14$. (The flour total is $4\times3+5\times2=22$.)

questions.stem: Matrix $A$ is $2\times3$ and matrix $B$ is $3\times4$. Which statement is true?
questions.answer: $AB$ is $2\times4$, and $BA$ is not defined
questions.solution: A product is defined when the first matrix's columns equal the second matrix's rows. For $AB$: 3 columns and 3 rows, so it is defined and is $2\times4$. For $BA$: 4 columns and 2 rows, so it is not defined.

solve.answer: $AB$ is $2\times4$, and $BA$ is not defined
solve.work: AB: (2x3)(3x4) = 2x4. BA: (3x4)(2x3), inner 4 and 2 differ, so not defined.

questions.stem: What is the inverse of the matrix with rows $[2, 1]$ and $[5, 3]$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $2\times3-1\times5=1$. Swap the diagonal entries and change the signs of the others: rows $[3, -1]$ and $[-5, 2]$, divided by 1. Check: $2\times3+1\times(-5)=1$.

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: Adult tickets cost $a$ dollars and child tickets cost $c$ dollars. Two groups paid: 2 adults and 3 children paid 29 dollars, and 1 adult and 2 children paid 17 dollars. This is $AX=B$, where $A$ has rows $[2, 3]$ and $[1, 2]$, $X$ is the column with entries $a$ and $c$, and $B$ is the column with entries $29$ and $17$. Use the inverse of $A$ to find $c$, in dollars.
questions.solution: The determinant of $A$ is $2\times2-3\times1=1$, so $A^{-1}$ has rows $[2, -3]$ and $[-1, 2]$. Then $c=(-1)\times29+2\times17=-29+34=5$. (And $a=2\times29-3\times17=7$; check $2\times7+3\times5=29$.)

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: A school sells adult tickets and child tickets. It solves a matrix equation with an inverse and gets 30 adult tickets and $-4$ child tickets. What does this tell the school?
choices: The model has an error, since tickets cannot be negative
The school sold 4 child tickets and also 30 adult tickets
The school sold 26 tickets in total, which is valid
The school sold 4 fewer child tickets than it planned
questions.answer: The model has an error, since tickets cannot be negative
questions.solution: A number of tickets cannot be negative, so a negative solution means the equations do not describe the real situation correctly (a wrong number or a wrong setup). It cannot be read as a count.

solve.answer: The model has an error, since tickets cannot be negative
solve.work: A negative count of tickets is impossible, so the model or its data contains an error.

questions.stem: A species has three age classes: young, middle, old. Each year, each middle animal has 2 offspring, each old animal has 1, and young animals have none. Half of the young survive to be middle, one fourth of the middle animals survive to be old, and old animals die. Now there are 100 young, 60 middle and 20 old. How many animals will there be in total next year?
questions.solution: Young next year: $2\times60+1\times20=140$. Middle: $\frac{1}{2}\times100=50$. Old: $\frac{1}{4}\times60=15$. Total: $140+50+15=205$.

questions.stem: A Leslie matrix has rows $[1, 2]$ and $[0.5, 0]$. The population vector (young, adult) is now $(40, 20)$. How many adults are there after two steps?
questions.solution: Step 1: young $=1\times40+2\times20=80$, adults $=0.5\times40=20$. Step 2: young $=80+2\times20=120$, adults $=0.5\times80=40$.

questions.stem: Each month, 10 percent of the people who ride the bus switch to the train, and 20 percent of the people who ride the train switch to the bus. This month 600 people ride the bus and 400 ride the train. How many people ride the bus next month?
questions.solution: Bus riders next month: the 90 percent of bus riders who stay, $0.9\times600=540$, plus the 20 percent of train riders who switch, $0.2\times400=80$. Total $620$.

questions.stem: A Markov chain has transition matrix with rows $[0.7, 0.3]$ and $[0.4, 0.6]$, where the entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the probability of moving from state $i$ to state $j$ in one step. Starting in state 1, what is the probability of being in state 1 after two steps?
questions.solution: Either stay in state 1 twice, $0.7\times0.7=0.49$, or go to state 2 and back, $0.3\times0.4=0.12$. Total $0.49+0.12=0.61$.

questions.stem: The matrix $N$ has rows [10, 4, 6] and [8, 5, 2]: the numbers of three products shipped to warehouse 1 and to warehouse 2. The column matrix $W$ has entries 3, 5 and 2, the weight in kilograms of one unit of each product. The product $NW$ gives the total weight shipped to each warehouse. What is the total weight shipped to warehouse 2, in kilograms?
questions.solution: Row 2 of $N$ times $W$: $8\times3+5\times5+2\times2=24+25+4=53$ kilograms.

questions.stem: Matrix $C$ is 4 by 3. For which size of matrix $D$ is the product $CD$ defined and 4 by 1?
questions.answer: 3 by 1
questions.solution: $CD$ is defined when the number of columns of $C$ (3) equals the number of rows of $D$. The product has the rows of $C$ (4) and the columns of $D$, so $D$ must have 3 rows and 1 column.

solve.answer: 3 by 1

questions.stem: Last month the sales of two products at two stores were the matrix with rows [20, 15] and [10, 30], with one row for each store and one column for each product. This month they were the matrix with rows [25, 10] and [12, 28]. Adding the two matrices gives the totals for the two months. How many units of product 1 were sold by the two stores over the two months together?
questions.solution: Product 1 is column 1 of each matrix. The two-month total adds $20+10$ from last month and $25+12$ from this month: $30+37=67$.

solve.work: Product 1 column: 20 + 10 + 25 + 12 = 67.

questions.stem: The matrix $S$ lists the scores of each student, one row per student, on each test, one column per test. The column matrix $W$ lists the weight of each test. What does the entry in row 3 of the product $SW$ tell us?
choices: student 3's weighted score over all the tests
the weighted score of every student on test 3
questions.answer: student 3's weighted score over all the tests
questions.solution: Row 3 of $S$ holds student 3's scores. Multiplying by $W$ multiplies each score by its test's weight and adds the results, a single weighted total for student 3.

solve.answer: student 3's weighted score over all the tests
solve.work: Row 3 of SW = sum of student 3's scores times the weights.

questions.stem: What is the inverse of the matrix with rows [4, 2] and [3, 2]?
questions.solution: The determinant is $4\times2-2\times3=2$. Swap the diagonal entries and change the signs of the others to get rows [2, -2] and [-3, 4], then divide by 2: rows [1, -1] and [-1.5, 2].

questions.stem: The matrix with rows [5, 3] and [k, 2] has determinant 4. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $5\times2-3k=10-3k$. Setting $10-3k=4$ gives $3k=6$, so $k=2$.

questions.stem: The matrix $A$ has rows [2, 3] and [1, 4]. What is the entry in row 1, column 2 of $A^{-1}$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $2\times4-3\times1=5$. The inverse is $\frac{1}{5}$ times the matrix with rows [4, -3] and [-1, 2], so row 1, column 2 is $-\frac{3}{5}$.

questions.stem: Which statement about the matrix with rows [6, 9] and [2, 3] is correct?
choices: It has an inverse, because $6\times3+9\times2=36$ is not 0
It has an inverse, because all of its entries are nonzero
It has no inverse, because its two rows are different
questions.answer: It has no inverse, because $6\times3-9\times2=0$
questions.solution: The determinant is $6\times3-9\times2=18-18=0$, so the matrix has no inverse. (Row 1 is 3 times row 2.) Having nonzero entries or different rows does not decide it.

solve.answer: It has no inverse, because $6\times3-9\times2=0$
solve.work: det = 18 - 18 = 0, so no inverse.

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: A rental company charges one daily price for every car and one for every van. Renting 2 cars and 1 van costs 190 dollars a day, and renting 1 car and 2 vans costs 230 dollars a day. Write this as $AX = B$ with $A$ having rows [2, 1] and [1, 2], and use $A^{-1}$ to find the daily price of one van, in dollars.
questions.solution: The determinant is $2\times2-1\times1=3$, so $A^{-1}$ has rows $\frac{1}{3}[2, -1]$ and $\frac{1}{3}[-1, 2]$. The van price is $\frac{1}{3}(-190+2\times230)=\frac{270}{3}=90$ dollars. (A car costs 50 dollars.)

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: The inverse of $A$ has rows [3, -1] and [-2, 1], and $B$ is the column with entries 4 and 5. Which column is $X = A^{-1}B$?
questions.answer: the column with entries 7 and -3
questions.solution: Row 1: $3\times4+(-1)\times5=7$. Row 2: $(-2)\times4+1\times5=-3$. Each entry of $X$ uses a ROW of the inverse times the column $B$.

solve.answer: the column with entries 7 and -3

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: Solve $3x + 4y = 18$ and $x + 2y = 8$ by using the inverse of the coefficient matrix. What is $y$?
questions.solution: The coefficient matrix has rows [3, 4] and [1, 2] and determinant $6-4=2$, so its inverse has rows [1, -2] and [-0.5, 1.5]. Then $y=-0.5\times18+1.5\times8=-9+12=3$. (And $x=18-24+... $ check: $x=1\times18-2\times8=2$, and $3\times2+4\times3=18$.)

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: Three adult tickets and 2 child tickets cost 26 dollars, and 1 adult ticket and 4 child tickets cost 22 dollars. With $X$ the column of the adult price $a$ and the child price $c$, which matrix equation describes this?
choices: rows [3, 2] and [1, 4] times the column $(a, c)$ equals the column $(26, 22)$
rows [3, 1] and [2, 4] times the column $(a, c)$ equals the column $(26, 22)$
rows [3, 2] and [1, 4] times the column $(a, c)$ equals the column $(22, 26)$
rows [3, 2] and [4, 1] times the column $(a, c)$ equals the column $(26, 22)$
questions.answer: rows [3, 2] and [1, 4] times the column $(a, c)$ equals the column $(26, 22)$
questions.solution: Each row holds the numbers of adult and child tickets in one purchase, in the order of $X$: [3, 2] and [1, 4]. The totals 26 and 22 go in $B$ in the same order as the rows.

solve.answer: rows [3, 2] and [1, 4] times the column $(a, c)$ equals the column $(26, 22)$

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: A farmer has 60 acres. A matrix model for planting gives 40 acres of corn and 25 acres of beans. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: The plan uses 15 acres less than is available, so 15 acres stay unplanted
The plan needs 65 acres, more than the 60 available, so the model or its numbers must be rechecked
The plan is fine, because each crop alone uses fewer than 60 acres
The plan is fine, because 40 + 25 = 65 is more than the land
questions.answer: The plan needs 65 acres, more than the 60 available, so the model or its numbers must be rechecked
questions.solution: The crops together need $40+25=65$ acres, but only 60 exist, so the solution cannot be carried out. The model or its data has a mistake.

solve.answer: The plan needs 65 acres, more than the 60 available, so the model or its numbers must be rechecked
solve.work: 40 + 25 = 65 > 60: infeasible, recheck.

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: Solving a matrix model gives $X = A^{-1}B$ as the column with entries 12 and 8: the numbers of adult and child riders on a bus. Adults pay 5 dollars and children pay 3 dollars. What is the total of the fares, in dollars?
questions.solution: Adults pay $12\times5=60$ dollars and children pay $8\times3=24$ dollars, so the total is 84 dollars.

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: Two students solve the same equation $AX = B$ and get the columns $(3, 5)$ and $(5, 3)$. How can the group tell which is correct?
choices: Add the entries of each column and pick the larger sum
Multiply each column by $B$ and see which product equals $A$
Multiply $A$ by each column and see which product equals $B$
Find the inverse of each column and compare it with $A$
questions.answer: Multiply $A$ by each column and see which product equals $B$
questions.solution: A solution must satisfy the equation, so check by substituting: compute $AX$ for each $X$ and see which gives $B$. The sums of entries are equal here and say nothing.

solve.answer: Multiply $A$ by each column and see which product equals $B$
solve.work: Substitute: check which X gives AX = B.

questions.stem: A Leslie matrix has rows [0.5, 1.5] and [0.4, 0]. The population vector (young, adult) is now $(100, 50)$. How many animals in total will there be next year?
questions.solution: Young next year: $0.5\times100+1.5\times50=50+75=125$. Adults next year: $0.4\times100=40$. Total: $125+40=165$.

questions.stem: A population has three age classes. Class 1 animals have no offspring, each class 2 animal has 2 offspring per year, and each class 3 animal has 4. Half of class 1 survive to class 2 and half of class 2 survive to class 3. Class 3 animals do not survive the year. Now the classes hold 50, 40 and 10 animals. How many animals will be in class 1 next year?
questions.solution: Class 1 next year is all the newborns: $2\times40+4\times10=80+40=120$.

solve.work: Class 1 next = 2 x 40 + 4 x 10 = 120.

questions.stem: A Leslie matrix has rows [0, 3] and [0.5, 0], and the population vector (young, adult) is now $(20, 30)$. How many adults are there after two years?
questions.solution: After one year: young $=3\times30=90$ and adults $=0.5\times20=10$. After two years: adults $=0.5\times90=45$ (and young $=3\times10=30$).

questions.stem: A Leslie matrix has rows [0, 4] and [0.25, 0]. What happens to the population vector after two years?
choices: It is four times as large
It is the same as at the start
questions.answer: It is the same as at the start
questions.solution: Multiplying the matrix by itself gives rows [1, 0] and [0, 1], since $4\times0.25=1$. Two steps multiply the population vector by the identity matrix, which leaves it unchanged.

solve.answer: It is the same as at the start
solve.work: L^2 = [[0.25x4,0],[0,4x0.25]] = I, so the vector returns to the start.

questions.stem: Each year 5 percent of the 8000 people living in a city move to the suburbs, and 3 percent of the 12000 people living in the suburbs move to the city. How many people live in the city next year?
questions.solution: The city loses $0.05\times8000=400$ people and gains $0.03\times12000=360$ people. $8000-400+360=7960$.

questions.stem: A machine is in one of three conditions each week: good, fair or poor, in that order. The transition matrix has rows [0.5, 0.5, 0], [0.2, 0.6, 0.2] and [0, 0.5, 0.5], where the entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the probability of moving from condition $i$ to condition $j$. This week the machine is good. What is the probability that it is poor two weeks from now?
questions.solution: To get from good to poor in two weeks, the machine must pass through fair (good to poor directly is impossible, and so is staying good then jumping to poor): $0.5\times0.2=0.1$. The other routes, through good or poor, have probability 0.

solve.work: Step 1 from good: (0.5,0.5,0). Poor at step 2: 0.5x0 + 0.5x0.2 + 0x0.5 = 0.1.

questions.stem: The transition matrix of a Markov chain has rows [0.9, 0.1] and [0.2, 0.8]. The probability vector $(p, q)$ is $(0.6, 0.4)$ now, and one step later it is $(p, q)$ times the matrix. What is it one step later?
questions.solution: New $p=0.6\times0.9+0.4\times0.2=0.54+0.08=0.62$ and new $q=0.6\times0.1+0.4\times0.8=0.06+0.32=0.38$. The two numbers add to 1, as probabilities must.

questions.stem: A Markov chain has three states. Its transition matrix has rows [0.5, 0.5, 0], [0, 0.5, 0.5] and [0.5, 0, 0.5], where the entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the probability of moving from state $i$ to state $j$ in one step. Starting in state 1, what is the probability of being in state 3 after two steps?
questions.solution: From state 1 the chain goes to state 1 or state 2, each with probability 0.5, and never straight to state 3. The path 1 to 1 to 3 has probability $0.5\times 0=0$. The path 1 to 2 to 3 has probability $0.5\times 0.5=0.25$. So the answer is 0.25.

solve.work: Two-step probability from state 1 to state 3 = (row 1 of P) . (column 3 of P) = 0.5*0 + 0.5*0.5 + 0*0.5 = 0.25.

questions.stem: A factory makes products X and Y. The matrix $M$ has rows $[2, 3]$ (product X) and $[4, 1]$ (product Y); the columns are units of steel and units of plastic needed for one item. Steel costs 5 dollars per unit and plastic costs 2 dollars per unit, written as the column matrix with entries $5$ and $2$. The factory makes 10 of X and 20 of Y. Using the product of the row matrix $[10, 20]$, $M$ and the cost column, find the total cost of materials in dollars.
questions.solution: Cost of one X: $2\times5+3\times2=16$. Cost of one Y: $4\times5+1\times2=22$. Total: $10\times16+20\times22=160+440=600$.

questions.stem: The matrix $A$ has rows $[3, 1]$ and $[4, 2]$. What is the bottom-right entry of its inverse $A^{-1}$?
questions.solution: The determinant is $3\times2-1\times4=2$. The inverse is $\frac{1}{2}$ times the matrix with rows $[2, -1]$ and $[-4, 3]$, so its bottom-right entry is $\frac{3}{2}$.

questions.stem: For which value of $k$ does the matrix with rows $[k, 3]$ and $[2, 6]$ have no inverse?
questions.solution: No inverse means determinant 0: $6k-3\times2=0$, so $6k=6$ and $k=1$.

solve.work: det = 6k - 6 = 0 gives k = 1.

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: A shop sells pens and notebooks. 2 pens and 3 notebooks cost 12 dollars, and 4 pens and 5 notebooks cost 22 dollars. Write this as $AX=B$ with $A$ having rows $[2, 3]$ and $[4, 5]$, where $X$ holds the price of a pen and then the price of a notebook, and solve it with $A^{-1}$. What is the cost of one notebook, in dollars?
questions.solution: The determinant is $2\times5-3\times4=-2$, so $A^{-1}=\frac{1}{-2}$ times rows $[5, -3]$ and $[-4, 2]$. The notebook price is $\frac{(-4)(12)+2(22)}{-2}=\frac{-4}{-2}=2$. (A pen costs 3 dollars: $2\times3+3\times2=12$ and $4\times3+5\times2=22$.)

questions.skill: Solving a system with an inverse matrix
questions.stem: A student tries to solve $2x+4y=6$ and $x+2y=5$ by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix. Why does this method fail?
choices: The coefficient matrix has determinant 10, which is too large to invert
The coefficient matrix is not square, so it has no inverse
The coefficient matrix has determinant 0, so it has no inverse
The constants 6 and 5 are different, so no matrix equation exists
questions.answer: The coefficient matrix has determinant 0, so it has no inverse
questions.solution: The coefficient matrix has rows $[2, 4]$ and $[1, 2]$, with determinant $2\times2-4\times1=0$. A matrix with determinant 0 has no inverse, so $X=A^{-1}B$ cannot be used.

solve.answer: The coefficient matrix has determinant 0, so it has no inverse
solve.work: det = 2*2 - 4*1 = 0, so the coefficient matrix is singular.

questions.skill: Interpreting the results of a matrix model
questions.stem: A warehouse ships small boxes and large boxes. With $s$ small and $l$ large boxes, $3s+2l=170$ and $s+l=65$, so $AX=B$ with $A$ having rows $[3, 2]$ and $[1, 1]$. Solve with $A^{-1}$. A small box weighs 4 kilograms and a large box weighs 7 kilograms. What is the total weight of the boxes in kilograms?
questions.solution: The determinant of $A$ is $3-2=1$, so $A^{-1}$ has rows $[1, -2]$ and $[-1, 3]$. Then $s=170-130=40$ and $l=-170+195=25$. Weight: $40\times4+25\times7=160+175=335$ kilograms.

questions.stem: A species has three age classes. Age-1 animals have no offspring, each age-2 animal has 4 offspring per year, and each age-3 animal has 2. Each year 60 percent of age-1 animals survive to age 2 and 30 percent of age-2 animals survive to age 3; age-3 animals do not survive. Which is the Leslie matrix?
questions.solution: The top row holds the offspring per animal of each age: $0$, $4$, $2$. Below it, survival from age 1 to 2 ($0.6$) sits in row 2, column 1, and survival from age 2 to 3 ($0.3$) in row 3, column 2.

solve.work: Top row fecundities [0,4,2]; survival on subdiagonal: 0.6 at (2,1), 0.3 at (3,2).

questions.stem: A population has two age classes, young and adult. Each adult has 2 young per year, and half of the young survive to become adults; adults die after one year. After one year there are 60 young and 20 adults. How many animals were there in total at the start?
questions.solution: Young now $=2\times$ (adults before), so there were $60\div2=30$ adults. Adults now $=\frac{1}{2}\times$ (young before), so there were $20\times2=40$ young. Total: $30+40=70$.

solve.work: Leslie [[0,2],[0.5,0]]. Young after = 2*A0 = 60 so A0 = 30; adults after = 0.5*Y0 = 20 so Y0 = 40. Total 70.

questions.stem: Each month, 20 percent of the customers of brand A switch to brand B, and 10 percent of the customers of brand B switch to brand A. In the long run, what fraction of the customers use brand A?
questions.solution: In the long run the number switching from A to B equals the number switching from B to A: $0.2a=0.1b$, so $b=2a$. Then $a+b=3a=1$, and brand A has $\frac{1}{3}$ of the customers.

solve.work: Steady state: flow A->B equals B->A: 0.2a = 0.1b, b = 2a, a + b = 1 so a = 1/3.

questions.stem: A Markov chain has transition matrix with rows $[0.5, 0.5]$ and $[0.2, 0.8]$. Which probability vector $(p, q)$ is the steady state, meaning that $(p, q)$ times the matrix gives $(p, q)$ again?
questions.answer: $\left(\frac{2}{7}, \frac{5}{7}\right)$
questions.solution: Solve $0.5p+0.2q=p$ with $p+q=1$: $0.2q=0.5p$, so $q=2.5p$ and $3.5p=1$, giving $p=\frac{2}{7}$ and $q=\frac{5}{7}$. Check: $\frac{2}{7}\times0.5+\frac{5}{7}\times0.2=\frac{2}{7}$.

solve.answer: $\left(\frac{2}{7}, \frac{5}{7}\right)$
